'''Mahendra Kumar Verma''' (born 27 May 1966) is an Indian physicist and professor at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]] who works on [[fluid dynamics]], [[turbulence]], and [[nonlinear dynamics]]. Verma earned his bachelor's degree in computer science from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] in 1988, and a Ph.D. in physics from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1994. He was awarded the [[Swarnajayanti Fellowship]] by the Department of Science and Technology, [[Government of India]] in 2006, and the [[A. P. J. Abdul Kalam|Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam]] [[Cray]] [[High-performance computing|HPC]] award, which honors high-performance computing contributions from India, in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/new/dr-mahendra-k-verma | title=Mahendra K. Verma |access-date=2017-03-12 |publisher=[[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2nd Annual Awards Honor HPC Contributions in India |url=https://www.cray.com/blog/2nd-annual-awards-honor-hpc-contributions-india/ |publisher=[[Cray|Cray Inc.]] |accessdate=3 August 2019 |date=29 May 2018 |archive-date=3 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803210547/https://www.cray.com/blog/2nd-annual-awards-honor-hpc-contributions-india/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is also an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows Elected 2019 |url=http://insaindia.res.in/pdf/IndFellows2020.pdf |publisher=[[Indian National Science Academy]] |accessdate=2 August 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802215436/http://insaindia.res.in/pdf/IndFellows2020.pdf |archivedate=2 August 2019}}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellow Profile |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Verma,_Prof._Mahendra_Kumar |publisher=[[Indian Academy of Sciences]] |accessdate=23 April 2020 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200423122443/https://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Verma,_Prof._Mahendra_Kumar |archivedate=23 April 2020}}</ref>
